modules.scope: NocoBase3 应用客户端的挂载路径解析、运行时配置与插件/Settings 路由注册；用于解释 /main 挂载下插件页面基址为何与宿主不一致。
modules.limitations: 未阅读 @nocobase/app-portal-sdk 源码（快照不含该包），其内部基址解析只由插件 dist 与应用兼容注释间接确认；未评测主题/样式一致性。

requirements.need: 应用在 /main 挂载下，所有插件 Settings 页与业务页都要用同一 API 基址。
requirements.responsibility: 框架负责把服务端决定的挂载路径一致地发布给所有客户端运行时；插件负责在自身客户端使用该来源。
requirements.recommendedUsage: app-client 公开 resolveAppBase()/resolveAppUrl()，以服务端渲染的 app.basePath 为唯一来源。
requirements.actualUsage: app-client 页面正常；AI KB 等基于 portal-sdk 的插件页读到 window.NOCOBASE_API_URL 回退 /api，应用加 api-base-compat.ts 回填才对齐。

requirements.need: 插件以声明式方式贡献 Settings 路由与组件覆盖。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供注册契约与路由合并；插件提供页面组件。
requirements.actualUsage: AI KB、api-keys 等插件均按此注册，路由可达；失败集中在数据请求基址而非注册。

requirementFit.reason: 注册与运行时配置入口可用，但两条客户端运行时对挂载路径不一致，插件 Settings 页在 /main 下 404，需求只能靠应用兼容层绕行。

usability.reason: resolveAppBase/resolveAppUrl 与 defineSettingsRoutes 语义清晰；但缺少“第三方插件客户端如何取得基址”的公开约定，接入方需自行发现不变量。

agentFriendliness.reason: 框架指引未说明 portal-sdk 客户端读 window.NOCOBASE_API_URL，Agent 只能从 404 反推并手写兼容模块；引导恢复成本高。

design.reason: 以服务端渲染配置为单一事实来源、未提供配置即抛错的设计合理；缺口在生态插件未共享该来源。

reliability.reason: 宿主自身解析稳定，但公开契约在插件组合下失效（/main 下插件请求 /api 404），实现未对不一致的基址给出检测或降级。

modules.limitations: 包只提供 dist 与 Registry 源码，未含 app-portal-sdk；真实向量化/问答受外部条件限制，本次只评接入与页面可用性。

modules.name: 文件附件与 OOXML 预览
modules.scope: @nocobase/app-plugin-file 的附件内容访问与 Registry 组件 UI 的 PNG/DOCX 预览，以及文件 Skill 的格式矩阵与验证要求；对应 B06。
modules.limitations: 未运行真实浏览器复现；DOCX 无头渲染超时为环境相关，无法在只读快照内判定 headed 生产环境是否稳定。

requirements.need: 工单内上传 PNG/DOCX，刷新后预览真实内容，损坏文件给出真实失败反馈。
requirements.responsibility: 插件提供内容访问、格式识别与本地 OOXML 渲染组件；应用负责关联与权限。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 复用 Registry component-ui 的 FilePreviewDialog；contentUrl 由 HTTP 补主机/挂载前缀。
requirements.actualUsage: Agent 采用 Registry 组件；第 4 轮 DOCX 停在 Loading，第 5 轮 headed 下正常渲染，无头下 20s 超时并显示“took too long”。

requirements.need: 渲染失败时给出可见错误与下载回退，而不是无限加载。
requirements.responsibility: 插件提供错误/降级 UI；应用负责调用。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 渲染错误走 OfficeOpenXmlDownloadFallback；无 url 时显示加载中。
requirements.actualUsage: 组件对 error 有回退，但渲染器未回调解析期间无超时，Loading 可能无限持续，正是第 4 轮观察。

requirementFit.reason: PNG/DOCX 上传、关联、内容访问与本地 OOXML 预览齐备，最终验收通过；渲染可用性受无头环境限制。

usability.reason: Registry 组件可直接复用、格式自动识别；但缺渲染超时/强降级，失败时可能长期停留在 Loading，排查成本高。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 明确列出格式矩阵、同源凭据与真实文件验证要求，Agent 能据此定位第 4 轮为渲染而非上传问题。

design.reason: contentUrl + 同源凭据 + 错误/下载回退的边界清晰，OOXML 本地渲染避免第三方服务。

reliability.reason: 正常路径可靠并已验收；渲染器解析失败/不回调时缺少超时兜底，会与测试要求的“真实失败反馈”冲突。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Implemented the device after-sales service and inspection collaboration system as an application-owned feature: one migration creating nine service collections, a service layer (access, ledger, tickets, inspections, knowledge, dashboard, notifications, bootstrap sample data), authenticated HTTP routes under /api/service, a Workflow package for idempotent ticket acceptance, Scheduler jobs, API-key device-platform endpoints, an AI Employee service assistant with a knowledge-lookup tool, and end-to-end tests against real migrated SQLite plus a booted standalone server. A later verification repair completed the shell test fixture after a notification bell was added to the header.

blockers.title: Application provider crashed in minimal and pre-migration runtimes
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed three cases: `Service "@nocobase/app/authorization" is not registered` in one, and `RepositoryError: Collection "serviceCustomers" does not exist` in two.
blockers.rootCause: ServiceApplicationProvider.boot() unconditionally resolved the optional authorization and user-administration tokens, and ServiceBootstrap.run() wrote sample data without checking that the application's own migration had created the service tables. A minimal test runtime registers neither plugin, and an embedded app whose database directory has no application migrations has no service tables.
blockers.resolution: boot() now only runs the bootstrap when both optional tokens are present in the container, and ServiceBootstrap.run() checks `db.builder().hasCollection('serviceCustomers')` before the sample-data phase (accounts and roles are still provisioned). All 44 test files / 331 tests pass.

blockers.title: Ticket keyword search raised a runtime repository error
blockers.symptom: `RepositoryError: Filter group "string" does not match Field "description" of type "text"` when listing tickets with a keyword; live ticket search would return 500.
blockers.rootCause: The ticket list filter used `filter.string('description').includes(...)` against a `text` column. Filter groups are typed by declared field type and the mismatch only fails at execution time.
blockers.resolution: Switched to `filter.text('description').includes(keyword, { mode: 'insensitive' })` and added the matching `text(path)` method to the hand-written filter type stub. Covered by tests/logic/service-business.test.ts.

blockers.title: Workflow auto-enable has no public API
blockers.symptom: The acceptance Workflow package loads but is disabled; there is no exported WorkflowRepository, no `enable` CLI command, and no auto-enable config, so a normal trigger would not run.
blockers.rootCause: Enablement state is stored in the workflow plugin's own tables and the plugin exposes no public contract for source-managed packages to declare themselves enabled.
blockers.resolution: The accept endpoint triggers the workflow with `{ manually: true, waitForCompletion: true }` and falls back to the idempotent service-level `acceptTicket` if no run is produced. Acceptance stays idempotent (one state change, one notification) whichever path executes.

blockers.title: Acceptance Workflow run nodes failed at runtime
blockers.symptom: The accept endpoint produced a Workflow run, but every run node logged `Instruction "run" failed`: `Cannot find module .../server/accept.js` in development, and `Cannot find module .../workflows/services/contracts.js` from the materialized production Artifact. The failed run recorded no business effect and QA found 0 successful runs.
blockers.rootCause: Two independent causes. (1) Run modules imported siblings with `.js` specifiers, which Node native TypeScript stripping does not map back to `.ts` in development. (2) The production Workflow Artifact is a self-contained copy under `storage/workflows/<key>/<digest>`; relative imports escape the copy root, and `ServiceContainer` matches bindings by token object identity, so a copy of `contracts.js` would also create a second token the application container never registered.
blockers.resolution: Run modules import siblings with `.ts` specifiers (rewritten to `.js` by `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` for the Artifact) and read application service tokens from a process-wide `globalThis` registry (`Symbol.for("nb3-factory.service-token-registry")`). The application creates each token once in `server/services/service-token.ts`; the workflow-local `server/workflows/ticket-acceptance/server/service-tokens.ts` returns the identical object. Verified in development (Node loading the `.ts` source) and against the compiled Artifact copied outside `node_modules`: both run nodes execute and `summarizeAcceptance` records the resulting status.

blockers.title: Header notification bell broke the baseline shell layout test fixture
blockers.symptom: Three tests in tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'resolve')` from `useService` -> `useApiClient` -> `NotificationInAppProvider`.
blockers.rootCause: The in-app notification bell was added to `HeaderActions`, which every shell layout renders. `NotificationInAppProvider` resolves `apiClientToken` and `realtimeClientToken` from `app.services`, but the layout-i18n test fixture built a partial `ClientApplication` with only `config` and `runtime`. tests/logic/client-shell.test.tsx had already been updated with those two tokens; this fixture was missed.
blockers.resolution: Added a service map with `apiClientToken` and `realtimeClientToken` to the layout-i18n `setup()` fixture, matching client-shell.test.tsx, so the real bell keeps rendering while the shell translation assertions stay unchanged. Re-ran tests/components plus the client-shell and client-runtime logic tests: 18 files / 143 tests pass; prettier and eslint clean on the changed test file.

blockers.title: DOCX repair-report preview could hang on 'Loading preview...' with no canvas and no error
blockers.symptom: Engineer Alpha opened ticket #1's Repair attachments, previewed the uploaded sample.docx, and the `data-office-open-xml-format=docx` container stayed empty (html length 284, no canvas/img) showing 'Loading preview...' for 25 s with no console error. GET /api/service/tickets/1/attachments/3/content and the docx chunk both returned 200.
blockers.rootCause: The docx viewer was created with `progressiveLayout: true`. In that mode `@silurus/ooxml` disables its own parse watchdog (`timeoutMs: false`) and resolves `load()` only when the progressive-layout scheduler publishes a preview; if that never arrives, `load()` stays pending forever and the component had no timeout of its own — unlike the sibling `OfficePreview`, which is bounded. The stall was not reproducible here: the library standalone, the production chunk, the full UI as admin and Engineer Alpha, eight cold-context runs, four viewports, CPU 20x plus slow-network throttling, an rAF stub and the exact QA browser tool all rendered a canvas (html length ~1922). The defect is a stalled progressive parse with no watchdog, reachable only under the QA run's conditions.
blockers.resolution: `OfficeOpenXmlPreview` now wraps `viewer.load()` in `withLoadTimeout` (20 s) which rejects with a distinct `OfficeOpenXmlTimeoutError`, rendering the existing download fallback instead of spinning forever, and `progressiveLayout: true` was removed from the docx and pptx viewers so the library's parse watchdog stays active and `load()` resolves once layout completes. Verified: a non-progressive standalone render produces a canvas in ~250 ms; `tests/components/file-preview.test.tsx` gained a stalled-viewer case asserting the loading state is replaced by the timeout fallback; client and server typecheck clean.

blockers.title: Manual 'Run daily jobs now' bypassed the Scheduler, so Trigger count stayed 0 and no execution records were written
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/inspections/run-daily returned 200 and generated inspection rows, but the plan detail still showed 'Trigger count 0' / 'No triggers have started.', /api/schedules reported runCount 0 and completedCount 0 for both plans, and /schedules/:id/occurrences was empty.
blockers.rootCause: The run-daily handler called `InspectionService.generateDueInspections()` and `remindOverdueTickets()` directly. Those are the Scheduler targets, so the business effects were correct, but nothing dispatched the Scheduler's own `ScheduleDispatchJob`, so no `schedule_occurrences` row and no `queue_schedules.run_count` update were written. The Scheduler's public service exposes no trigger, and `queueManagerToken.dispatch()` cannot set the `scheduleId` the job requires.
blockers.resolution: Added an application-owned `SchedulerRunService` (`server/services/scheduler-run-service.ts`) that lists the Scheduler's schedules, skips missing/disabled ones, triggers each active schedule through the Queue package's public `Schedule.trigger()` — the same call the Queue worker makes for a due schedule, which sets `scheduleId` and increments `runCount`/`lastRunAt` — then polls that schedule's occurrences for the new id and returns the occurrence's real status and `resultSummary`. `POST /inspections/run-daily` now calls `runAll([inspection, reminder])` and returns `{ generation, reminders, executions }`; the inspections page shows success only when every execution succeeded, otherwise an error toast naming the Scheduler statuses. Re-verified in `tests/logic/service-routes.test.ts`: the supervisor run returns two `succeeded` executions with occurrence ids, `schedule_occurrences` has a `succeeded` row and `queue_schedules.run_count >= 1`, while the engineer still gets 403. Idempotency is preserved because the targets deduplicate per device/ticket and day.

blockers.title: Settings > Knowledge bases page 404ed under the application mount path
blockers.symptom: Under `/main`, Settings > Knowledge bases requested `/api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list` and showed "Unable to load this view / NocoBase request failed (404)", while `GET /main/api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list` returned 200 with an empty list. The other AI pages (LLM services, AI employees) already used `/main/api`.
blockers.rootCause: The AI Knowledge Base plugin's browser half talks to the server through `@nocobase/app-portal-sdk`'s `nocobaseClient`, a v2-era client that captures its API base URL once at module evaluation from `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` (falling back to `http://127.0.0.1:13000/api`). The v3 application shell instead reads the server-rendered `#nocobase-runtime-config` block (via `@nocobase/app-client`), so nothing populated `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` and the plugin requested the wrong base. The package also publishes no window value of its own.
blockers.resolution: Added `client/api-base-compat.ts`, imported first in `client/index.tsx` before any plugin (and therefore before the Portal SDK) is evaluated. It derives the mount path from `@nocobase/app-client`'s `resolveAppBase`/`resolveAppUrl` and sets `window.APP_BASE_PATH` and `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` once, only when an integrator has not set them, and stays silent on a page the application server did not render. The plugin's `pm:listEnabled` prerequisite gate is dead code (not mounted), so this alone fixes the Settings page. Covered by tests/logic/api-base-compat.test.ts.

blockers.title: Device-manual knowledge base was empty, with no supervisor upload or processing status
blockers.symptom: The Service Assistant had its knowledge-base toggle off and no knowledge base existed (count 0). Knowledge > Device manuals only showed the two built-in read-only manuals, and `GET /knowledge/manuals` returned slug/title/summary/content, so a supervisor had no entry to upload the manuals and no real processing status to read.
blockers.rootCause: The plugin's declarative manifest `init` operation requires an enabled vector database and an enabled LLM service by key (`requireReferences`), and none is configured (SQLite default; PGVector needs Postgres; no credentials). Nothing else in the application ever created the knowledge base, so the assistant had nothing to bind to and the page had nothing to show.
blockers.resolution: Added an idempotent application provider (`ManualKnowledgeBaseProvider` + `ManualKnowledgeBaseProvisioner`): it creates the LOCAL `device-manuals` knowledge base through the database when absent, writes the two manuals to the Drive, then ingests them through the plugin's public manifest `append` operation. Manifest `append` skips reference validation and records the real file/processing result, so failures surface instead of being hidden. The assistant is bound by merging `device-manuals` into `knowledgeBase.knowledgeBaseKeys` and setting `enableKnowledgeBase: true` via `AIManager.upsertEmployee`. Knowledge > Device manuals now lists the documents with their real `indexStatus`/error message and shows Upload / Retry / Remove to a supervisor only, behind an app-owned `GET /service/knowledge/manual-knowledge-base` `canManage` signal. Verified in tests/logic/service-routes.test.ts against a real migrated SQLite server: the base exists, two documents are ingested, the assistant record reports `enableKnowledgeBase: true` with the key, engineers get `canManage: false`, and anonymous callers get 401.

blockers.title: Real "update manual -> new assistant answer" acceptance cannot be completed in this environment
blockers.symptom: B11's strongest criterion - upload a manual, then observe a new assistant conversation answer from the updated content - cannot be demonstrated. Vectorization ends in the plugin's real ERROR/PENDING state because no vector database or embedding model resolves.
blockers.rootCause: No selectable vector database and no LLM service exist in this application (SQLite default; PGVector requires Postgres; no service credentials are available or permitted), so neither indexing nor model-backed answering can run. The task explicitly forbids substituting a fixed or faked answer for a completed result.
blockers.resolution: Recorded as blocked / not_run. The application shows the true processing status and reason instead of a fabricated success; the satisfied parts of B11 (Engineer Alpha has Read only, the assistant answers with citations within the reader's scope, an unmatched question returns an explicit 'No matching source', and an unavailable model reports local retrieval) are preserved. The two manuals are ingested through the public manifest path, so the acceptance becomes runnable unchanged once a vector database and model are configured.

improvements.title: Filter operator and field type mismatch is only caught at runtime
improvements.detail: Using a filter group that does not match a collection field's declared type compiles cleanly and throws RepositoryError at execution. This cost a live bug in ticket keyword search and is easy to repeat with text vs string columns.
improvements.suggestedChange: Derive the repository filter type from the declared collection metadata so `filter.text` / `filter.string` selection is checked by the compiler, or surface the mismatch as a startup/schema validation warning.

improvements.title: Workflow run scripts cannot share application modules or token instances
improvements.detail: A run script is loaded from a copied Artifact directory: relative imports escape the copy root, the copy is a separate module instance, and the Artifact may sit outside the server node_modules. `ServiceContainer` matches by token identity, so importing the application contracts module from a run script can never resolve a service even when the import loads. The failure only appears when the node first runs.
improvements.suggestedChange: Give the Workflow plugin a first-class way for an application-owned run script to receive application services (for example service instances in run options, or a documented global token-registry helper), and make the Workflow build reject a run module that imports outside its package root.

improvements.title: Partial ClientApplication fixtures must track new shell service dependencies
improvements.detail: Shell components are rendered across several tests, and each test builds its own `ClientApplication` fixture. When HeaderActions gained a plugin provider that reads `app.services`, only the fixtures that already supplied services kept working; the layout-i18n fixture silently lacked a `services` field that TypeScript could not require because the object is cast `as unknown as ClientApplication`.
improvements.suggestedChange: Provide a shared test helper that builds a `ClientApplication` fixture with the standard tokens (`apiClientToken`, `realtimeClientToken`, authentication/authorization) defaulted, and have shell tests spread overrides onto it, so adding a service-backed header component updates every fixture in one place.

improvements.title: No public trigger or read contract for source-managed Scheduler schedules
improvements.detail: The Scheduler's public service only advertises `registerTarget`/`defineSchedule`. An application that must trigger a schedule on demand has to reach through the Queue package's `Schedule.trigger()` and reconstruct the connection the queue is configured on from `config.queue`, then cast the service to read `list()`/`listOccurrences()`. The capability exists and works, but every application rebuilds the same undeclared interface and config lookup.
improvements.suggestedChange: Expose the Scheduler's already-implemented list/occurrence reads and a documented 'trigger this schedule now' operation on its public service (or routes), including resolution of the queue connection, so an application never has to reconstruct plugin internals from queue configuration.

improvements.title: Plugin browser code must not read its API base URL from a v2-only window global
improvements.detail: A plugin's browser half resolves the API base from `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` captured at module init (`@nocobase/app-portal-sdk`), while the v3 shell reads the server-rendered `#nocobase-runtime-config`. Under any non-root mount path the two disagree and the plugin 404s. The application had to add a first-import shim to republish the mount path before the plugin loads.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the Portal SDK client fall back to the same server-rendered runtime configuration the v3 shell uses (or read it lazily rather than capturing `API_URL` at module init), so a plugin works under any base path without an application shim.

improvements.title: AI Knowledge Base HTTP routes require authentication only, so role gating falls to the UI
improvements.detail: The plugin's routes install `authentication.required()` for the knowledge-base action paths but no authorization check, and `KnowledgeBaseDocumentService` hardcodes `accessAbility: 'readWrite'`. Any authenticated user can call create/upload/destroy over HTTP, so "engineers may not modify the knowledge base" can only be enforced by hiding controls in the application page - which is neither a security boundary nor discoverable from the plugin contract.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the plugin register authorization for its write actions (or expose a documented capability check), so an application can rely on the server rather than on which buttons it renders.

## Common contract

Base path: `/v2/api`. Route action URLs use `/<resource>:<action>`. All actions require authentication headers/cookies accepted by the App Authentication service. Missing user ID returns 401:

```json
{ "errors": [{ "message": "Authentication required" }] }
```

Success envelopes are `{"data": value}`. List helpers return:

```json
{ "data": { "data": [], "meta": { "count": 0, "page": 1, "pageSize": 20 } } }
```

Errors use `{"errors":[{"message":"..."}]}`. A thrown `status` is used; otherwise a message containing “not found” maps to 404 and other failures map to 500.

Pagination query: `page` default 1/min 1; `pageSize` default 20/min 1/max 200; `paginate=false` disables limit/offset. Lists are sorted by `-createdAt`; caller `sort` is ignored. ID readers accept `name`, `name[]`, repeated values, and comma-separated values.

Use an authenticated action client when possible:

```ts
await nocobaseClient.action('aiKnowledgeBase', 'list', {
  method: 'GET',
  query: { page: 1, pageSize: 20 },
  unwrap: 'none',
});
```

 * The AI Knowledge Base plugin's client talks to the server through

 * (and therefore before the Portal SDK) is loaded, and derives the same URL
 * from the configuration the server already published. Values set explicitly
 * by an integrator are left untouched, and a page that was not served by the

| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| DOCX / XLSX / PPTX                                   | Local `@silurus/ooxml` viewer     | Same-origin session credentials; no public URL or third-party service required |

evidence.excerpt:
Preview supports safe raster images, PDF via a fetched blob, text/Markdown and audio/video. HTML/SVG/XML previews and unsafe URL schemes are rejected. DOCX, XLSX and PPTX use lazily loaded `@silurus/ooxml` viewers to render locally from `FileRecord.contentUrl`; their content is not sent to a third-party preview service. Legacy DOC/XLS/PPT and OpenDocument formats use Office Online, which requires an internet-accessible absolute URL and cannot use the App session.

OOXML, PDF and text fetches use same-origin credentials. An App-owned content route protected by same-origin session cookies can therefore serve restricted previews, provided it checks the caller's record access. Cross-origin fetches omit credentials and require CORS; an external cookie-protected URL is not supported by this default path. The Repository API client's Bearer token is not automatically attached to content fetches.

For Bearer-only content authorization, adapt the installed Registry source in the App. Add an authenticated content loader to the OOXML fetch path and `PreviewBody`'s PDF/text fetches, and adapt download and media/image paths as needed. Resolve authentication through the App's supported client/session services and send credentials only to the trusted content endpoint. Do not put tokens in `contentUrl`. If the adapter creates blob URLs, keep an App-owned trusted URL set, pass it to the relevant `resolveSafeFileUrl` calls, and revoke URLs when replaced or unmounted. Merely assigning a `blob:` URL to `FileRecord.contentUrl` is insufficient: the default components reject untrusted blob URLs.

OOXML request or rendering failure displays an error and, when downloads are enabled, a download action. `download={false}` removes that action. This is not a second preview service or a guarantee that downloading the same inaccessible URL will succeed.

## Verify and handle failures

Verify upload → query → contentUrl → identical downloaded bytes, including batch upload, resource aliases and host prefixes. After materialization run the consuming App's typecheck/build and exercise upload, cancel/retry, remove, download and preview. Restricted files need anonymous, forbidden-user and permitted-user tests against both API and content routes. Inspectors check registration only.

For preview integration or changes, verify each of DOCX/XLSX/PPTX with real files in development and a served production build. Check relative same-origin URLs, an authorized and unauthorized session, cross-origin CORS success/failure, failed requests and invalid documents, and `download={false}`. Close or switch files while loading and after a failure: pending requests must abort, viewers must be destroyed, and the next file must render without stale state. Unit mocks and a successful build do not establish document rendering fidelity.

## Management Entry Points

The list page is `/settings/schedules`; details are at `/settings/schedules/:scheduleId`. Definitions are maintained in source. The UI supports viewing and enabling/disabling tasks, with no API for creating or editing Cron definitions.

All routes below require authentication and authorization for `{ resource: { type: 'page', id: 'scheduler.schedules' }, action: 'access' }`. Enabling/disabling currently uses the same permission, not a separate update action.

| Method and path                      | Response / effect                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/schedules`                 | `{ data: ScheduleListItem[] }`                                                                                |
| `GET /api/schedules/:id/occurrences` | `{ data: ScheduleOccurrenceView[] }`; currently at most the latest 100 records, with no pagination parameters |
| `POST /api/schedules/:id/enable`     | `{ data: ScheduleListItem }`; enables the task, no request body                                               |
| `POST /api/schedules/:id/disable`    | `{ data: ScheduleListItem }`; pauses the task, no request body                                                |

Use the id returned by list for `:id`, not the definition key or workflowKey. Enabling/disabling affects future scheduling; it does not cancel already dispatched Queue Jobs or workflows.

`schedulerServiceToken` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-scheduler/server/tokens` is the plugin's one public service, and it is a contribution surface rather than an administration one:

```ts
registerTarget<TConfig extends JsonObject>(
  target: ScheduleTargetType<TConfig>,
): ScheduleTargetHandle;

defineSchedule(definition: ScheduleDefinition): void;
```

The returned handle carries `reportCompletion(occurrenceId, reference, completion)`, and completes only occurrences its own target started. `defineSchedule` has no return value; it validates and stores the definition in the in-memory manifest consumed by the next sync.

Reading and changing schedules — list, occurrences, enable and disable — is reachable through the HTTP API above, and synchronization through `pnpm nocobase scheduler sync`. Neither is exposed as a resolvable service: the store, the target registry and the job dispatch table are private to the plugin, so an application cannot bypass the authorization its Routes enforce by resolving them from the container.

evidence.excerpt:
A sharing rule adds selected records, or a record access selection, for the subjects it lists, provided they already hold the action. Sharing does not grant the operation, fields, page access or related records, and it cannot select all records. Grants, default access and sharing combine first; restriction rules then narrow the result.

Read the installed `nocobase-app-plugin-authorization` Skill first for composite resources, data scopes, fields, server policy enforcement and inherited subjects. The package README at `node_modules/@nocobase/app-plugin-authz-sharing-rules/README.md` is the complete reference for the service, the HTTP routes and the exports; this Skill covers how to use them.

For sharing between departments, read the application development Skill's `references/organization/permission-design.md` first. A rule whose recipient is a department shares specific records with it; a viewer-relative department scope such as 本部门及下属部门 is computed for the viewer and cannot select another department's records. The guide's optional sharing section covers this plugin, and its core section says what remains with permission sets alone.

## Development workflow

1. Identify the real collaboration exception: who receives which records, for which actions, and why. Use explicit records for one handover; use a record access selection for a maintained region or team rule.
2. Grant the recipients the business action through a permission set first. Register inherited subjects and their active membership resolver through the main authorization Skill.
3. Inspect every data scope the operation requires. Quote submission needs the selected quote and its actual parent project. Add each action and data scope deliberately; view, edit and submit are different permissions.
4. Save a complete rule through the settings page or the service. Keep record ids tied to their data scope's collection and preserve the other entries on update.
5. Verify the handover works, an unshared parent still blocks the workflow, restrictions still exclude confidential records, and sharing alone cannot activate a missing operation.
6. Revoke the recipient or the team's permission set and verify the next request loses only that source. Independent direct-user sharing and direct assignments must survive.

Default access, sharing rules and restriction rules are optional plugins. Read their installed Skills when the business requirement calls for a common baseline, collaboration exception or record exclusion. If the corresponding Skill is absent, treat the capability as unsupported in this App and explain that it requires separate development. Do not assume its APIs, tables or seed format, or silently install/configure it. If the Skill exists, follow it to verify runtime activation and migrations. Implementation and seed details belong to that owning Skill. Do not implement replacement role tables or assume all optional plugins are present.

## Turn requirements into a matrix

Record actor/job, page, business operation, data scope, readable/writable fields, relation capabilities and administrator responsibilities. Use real jobs as permission sets and business relationships as scopes. Clarify material missing boundaries, such as whether a delegate can submit as well as edit, and whether a confidentiality restriction must cover every operation.
